update.title: Shared the active Wayland output with session services
update.summary: Built a Bash startup script that waits for Wayland, selects the first enabled output from wlr-randr, and publishes it through both systemd and a runtime file.

blocks.body:
## Publish one output name for the session

User services needed a Wayland connector name, but hardcoding one tied them to a particular display setup. I added a startup script that waits for the Wayland socket, asks `wlr-randr` for enabled outputs, and selects the first one marked `Enabled: yes`.

commands.output:
Detected primary monitor: DP-3
Exported: PRIMARY_MONITOR=DP-3
Wrote: /run/user/1000/primary-monitor

blocks.description: Representative output showing the environment and runtime-file forms of the detected connector.

blocks.body:
## Serve both systemd and file-based consumers

The script publishes the connector as `PRIMARY_MONITOR` in the systemd user environment and writes the same value to `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/primary-monitor`. Wallpaper Service reads the runtime file during startup, while other user services can consume the environment value after detection completes.

blocks.label: Wallpaper Service: a consumer of the detected output
